sources.facts: V2 contributes LP tokens through feeTo; V3/V4 use explicit collection adapters. This identifies an omitted asset class, not its value or a profitable exchange. The deployment table identifies canonical Ethereum V2 factory0x5c69bee701ef814a2b6a3edd4b1652cb9cc5aa6f. Runtime configuration still needs observation.

Fee liquidity uses integer roots of reserve product and kLast: S*(rootK-rootKLast)/(5*rootK+rootKLast), rounded down, if feeTo and kLast are nonzero and growth is positive. Mint and burn invoke this before reading updated supply. Mint requires positive user liquidity from deposited amounts; burn uses pair-held LP and actual underlying balances, and requires both outputs positive. Mint/burn update reserves and kLast. Sync and skim do not call the fee-mint helper. A full cycle therefore needs deposit capital, resource payment, successful transfers, exits and gas; accumulated fee LP is not free cash.

Factory getPair maps both token orders to the same created pair. Tokens are sorted and nonzero; feeTo is controlled by feeToSetter. Verify mapping at the chosen state instead of accepting a token label as LP identity.

LP units use18 decimals; supply and balances are explicit. Minting increases both, burning decreases both, and transfers preserve supply. These source facts do not prove runtime equivalence or underlying token behavior.
The iterative square root rounds down. Use exact integers, including fee and redemption floors.

selection: The first4 assets in the independently audited nonce1387 release list are candidate LPs. No identity, inventory, value or success is assumed. All20 listed assets receive jar balance reads. Prior release receipt was capped; that history remains unavailable for payouts or gas.
